Trial #1: New plan: I prematurely concluded the exploration with "DONE" while in the Balcony, failing to check if all reachable directions from the current node and previously visited nodes had been fully explored. Specifically, upon returning to the Balcony, I ignored the available "south" direction (which leads back to the Media room, potentially revealing new connections or confirming the map's completeness) and the "west" direction (which leads to the Guest room, where I might have missed a path). My strategy was flawed because I assumed the map was complete based on the number of unique rooms visited rather than verifying that every available direction from every visited room had been traversed. Next time, I will implement a strict "visited edges" check: before issuing "DONE", I must ensure that for every room in my `nodes` list, every direction listed as "available" in the history has been taken at least once. If I am in a room with available directions that I have not yet taken in the current session (or that lead to unexplored connections), I must take the untried direction instead of stopping. I will only stop when I am in a room where all available directions lead to already visited rooms and all edges between visited rooms have been confirmed.

New plan: The previous attempt failed because the JSON graph structure was malformed. Specifically, I included `null` as a destination in an edge tuple `("Craft room", null)` and incorrectly assigned the edge for the "north" move from the Craft room to the "north" list instead of the "west" list (since I arrived from the west). The format requires edges to be tuples of two valid room names `(source, destination)` and to be categorized under the direction that connects them. Next time, I will strictly ensure that: 1) Every edge tuple contains two existing room names from my `nodes` list, never `null`. 2) When moving from Room A to Room B via direction D, I add the tuple `(A, B)` to the `edges[D]` list. 3) I will double-check the JSON syntax (commas, quotes, brackets) before sending to ensure it is valid and strictly adheres to the provided example format.
